title: Monolith: when it is still the right call

videos.script: Every system has an architecture, whether somebody chose it or not. {{decisions}} It is the set of decisions that are expensive to change later. How the code is split. Where the data lives. What happens when a part fails. This course is about making those decisions on purpose. {{map}} It starts with the shape most systems begin with, and many keep: the monolith. One program, one deploy, one database. {{monolith}} You will build a small one, a grocery shop called Quitanda, on a machine of your own. {{lab}} You will watch it do something a distributed system finds very hard: change four things at once, or none of them. {{transaction}} And you will see where it starts to hurt. A deploy that carries everything. A copy of the whole program when only one part is busy. {{hurts}} By the end, you should be able to say when a monolith is still the right call, and what would have to change for it to stop being one.
